l4_steps.name: Capture safety occurrence report
l4_steps.input: Observed hazard, incident, near-miss, or unsafe condition
l4_steps.output: Safety occurrence record with initial classification and timestamp
l4_steps.kpi: Report submission rate ≥95% of known occurrences within 24 hrs
l4_steps.pain_point: Anonymous voluntary reporting culture varies by crew base; under-reporting persists in stations without dedicated Safety Officers

l4_steps.name: Classify report type & severity tier
l4_steps.output: Classified report: incident / hazard / near-miss / accident with initial severity tier (1–5)
l4_steps.kpi: Classification accuracy ≥98% validated at quarterly QA review
l4_steps.pain_point: Inconsistent severity tier assignment across regions; IQSMS taxonomy not always aligned with ICAO Annex 13 definitions

l4_steps.name: Determine mandatory regulatory reporting threshold
l4_steps.input: Classified occurrence record, FAR Part 830 / ICAO Annex 13 criteria matrix
l4_steps.output: Reporting decision: mandatory FAA/NTSB notification required (Y/N)
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of mandatory reports filed within regulatory deadlines (2 hrs / 10 days per FAR 830)
l4_steps.pain_point: Threshold ambiguity for ground damage events under FAR 830.5; legal and safety teams misalign on what constitutes 'substantial damage'

l4_steps.name: Submit voluntary report to ASAP/NASA ASRS
l4_steps.output: ASRS report number; ASAP event record filed with ASAP ERC (Event Review Committee)
l4_steps.kpi: ASAP programme participation rate ≥80% of eligible workforce
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA AC 120-66B ASAP MOU must be current; if MOU lapses, regulatory protection for reporters is void — high legal exposure

l4_steps.name: Initiate mandatory FAA/NTSB notification
l4_steps.input: Mandatory reporting decision from Step 1.3; occurrence facts
l4_steps.output: FAA/NTSB preliminary notification; ASIAS occurrence record; internal hold placed on aircraft/evidence
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of NTSB immediate notifications within 2 hrs of accident (FAR 830.5)
l4_steps.pain_point: Coordination latency between Operations Control and Safety when event occurs overnight; on-call Director of Safety pager escalation path not always followed

l4_steps.name: Assign risk probability & severity matrix score
l4_steps.input: Classified occurrence record; ICAO SMS risk matrix template
l4_steps.output: Risk index score (probability 1–5 × severity 1–5); initial risk colour: green/amber/red
l4_steps.kpi: Risk assessments completed within 48 hrs of report receipt for Tier 1–2 events
l4_steps.pain_point: Risk matrix calibration is subjective; two analysts rating same event can produce divergent scores without standardised anchor examples in IQSMS

l4_steps.name: Validate risk score at Safety Review Board
l4_steps.input: Risk index score from Step 2.1; FOQA data (if flight event)
l4_steps.output: Validated risk rating; escalation decision for red-rated risks
l4_steps.kpi: Safety Review Board convenes within 5 business days for red-rated risks
l4_steps.pain_point: Board quorum requires VP-level attendees; scheduling conflicts delay review for high-severity events; FOQA data retrieval from Teledyne SSFDR takes 48–72 hrs

l4_steps.name: Accept low risk & assign monitoring SPI
l4_steps.output: Safety Performance Indicator (SPI) assigned; monitoring threshold set in Tableau
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of accepted risks assigned at least one SPI within 5 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Tableau Safety BI dashboard is manually updated monthly; real-time SPI trending not available — latent risks may not surface until next board review

l4_steps.name: Initiate formal safety investigation
l4_steps.input: Escalated red/amber risk from Step 2.2; preliminary event facts
l4_steps.output: Investigation plan: scope, team, evidence list, timeline; IQSMS investigation record opened
l4_steps.kpi: Investigation plan issued within 24 hrs of escalation for Tier 1 events
l4_steps.pain_point: Investigator availability limited at outstations; company investigators are also line employees — release from duty requires crew scheduling coordination with Jeppesen Crew Management

l4_steps.name: Gather evidence including FOQA flight data
l4_steps.input: Flight identifier, tail number, date/time; investigation plan from Step 3.1
l4_steps.output: QAR/FOQA data extract; CVR/FDR preservation request (if applicable); witness statements in IQSMS
l4_steps.kpi: FOQA data retrieved within 72 hrs for flight-related events
l4_steps.pain_point: CVR/FDR data automatically overwritten after 30 days — late reporting of incidents frequently results in lost recorder data; preservation requests must be issued same day

l4_steps.name: Perform root cause analysis using bowtie/5-Whys
l4_steps.input: Evidence package from Step 3.2; FOQA data; witness statements
l4_steps.output: Root cause statement; contributing factors list; bowtie barriers analysis in IQSMS
l4_steps.kpi: Root cause identified for ≥90% of Tier 1 investigations within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: Bowtie analysis tool within IQSMS lacks integration with operational data — investigators manually cross-reference FOQA exports, increasing analysis time by 30–40%

l4_steps.name: Document investigation findings & close investigation
l4_steps.input: Root cause and contributing factors from Step 3.3
l4_steps.output: Final investigation report; linked corrective action records; report published in IQSMS
l4_steps.kpi: Investigation report issued within 60 days for Tier 1; 30 days for Tier 2
l4_steps.pain_point: Regulatory review of investigation reports by FAA/NTSB (if MOU-governed) can impose revisions — internal report may need to be amended post-publication, creating version control issues

l4_steps.name: Develop safety risk controls & mitigations
l4_steps.input: Investigation report from Step 3.4; risk residual score
l4_steps.output: Risk control plan: engineering controls, procedural changes, training interventions; residual risk target score
l4_steps.kpi: Risk residual score reduced to green (≤4) for ≥95% of Tier 1 events post-mitigation
l4_steps.pain_point: Procedural changes require FOM/GOM amendment workflow through Standards & Compliance — average revision cycle is 45–60 days, leaving residual risk unmitigated in the interim

l4_steps.name: Assign corrective action owners & due dates
l4_steps.output: Corrective action tasks assigned in IQSMS with responsible owner, priority, and target close date
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of corrective actions have named owner and due date within 5 days of investigation closure
l4_steps.pain_point: Cross-departmental corrective actions (e.g. Maintenance + Ops) lack shared accountability — IQSMS task ownership model does not enforce escalation when due dates slip

l4_steps.name: Verify corrective action effectiveness
l4_steps.input: Closed corrective action records; post-implementation SPI data from Tableau
l4_steps.output: Effectiveness verification record; risk formally closed or re-opened if recurrence detected
l4_steps.kpi: Corrective action on-time closure rate ≥85%; recurrence rate for closed risks <5% within 12 months
l4_steps.pain_point: Effectiveness verification relies on SPI trend analysis over 6–12 months — impatient leadership pressure to close risks prematurely inflates 'green' status without sufficient data

l4_steps.name: Track safety performance indicators vs targets
l4_steps.input: SPI data feeds from IQSMS, FOQA, ASAP, ASRS aggregation
l4_steps.output: Monthly SPI scorecard: accident rate, serious incident rate, FOQA exceedance rate, ASAP report volume
l4_steps.kpi: Accident rate: 0 per year; Serious incident rate ≤0.3 per 100,000 flights; FOQA exceedance rate ≤1.5%
l4_steps.pain_point: FOQA data pipeline from Teledyne SSFDR to Tableau requires manual CSV export — automated API integration not yet implemented, causing 5–10 day data lag

l4_steps.name: Publish monthly safety performance report to executives
l4_steps.input: SPI scorecard from Step 5.1; corrective action status from IQSMS
l4_steps.output: Executive safety performance report distributed via SharePoint; board safety committee briefing deck
l4_steps.kpi: Monthly report published by 10th of following month; 100% board safety committee attendance
l4_steps.pain_point: Board-level safety committee may lack aviation SMS expertise — safety reporting must translate technical SPI data into business risk language; skills gap in governance layer

l4_steps.name: Conduct scheduled SMS internal audit
l4_steps.input: FAA AC 120-92B SMS framework; annual audit schedule; previous audit findings
l4_steps.output: Audit findings report; non-conformances raised in IQSMS; corrective action requests issued
l4_steps.kpi: Annual SMS audit completion rate 100%; critical non-conformances closed within 30 days
l4_steps.pain_point: FAA AC 120-92B SMS requirements for Part 121 carriers are currently voluntary — without mandate, audit rigour is inconsistent and funding for SMS programme competes with operational priorities

l4_steps.name: Submit mandatory occurrence reports to FAA ASIAS
l4_steps.input: Mandatory occurrence records from Steps 1.3 and 1.5; Service Difficulty Reports (SDRs) from Maintenance
l4_steps.output: ASIAS submission receipts; SDR filings; MOR (Malfunction or Defect Report) records archived
l4_steps.kpi: 100% of SDRs filed within 3 days of discovery (FAR 121.703); zero overdue mandatory reports
l4_steps.pain_point: SDR filing workflow spans Maintenance and Safety departments — coordination gaps between AMOS MRO system and IQSMS mean some defects are resolved without triggering the SDR filing check
